                         JOINT INITIAL BRIEF OF
                     WILLIAMSON COUNTY, TEXAS AND
            THE WILLIAMSON COUNTY CONSERVATION FOUNDATION

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

       COMES NOW, Williamson County, Texas (hereinafter referred to as “Williamson

County”) and the Williamson County Conservation Foundation (hereinafter referred to as

“WCCF”), Intervenors in the above-captioned cause, and file their Joint Initial Brief expressing

opposition against the specific routes and links identified herein, which would have a significant

negative impact on both Williamson County and WCCF properties and projects if approved.

       On May 12, 2026, Williamson County filed its Statement of Position, identifying the

following links that would traverse or materially interfere with areas in Williamson County used

for existing and future transportation infrastructure projects: B3, D2, E3, E4, F01, F02, F04, F7,

F8, F24, F33, F34, F41, F42, F43, F44, F45, G9, G11, G31, G41, and G81. On May 12, 2026,

WCCF filed a Statement of Position and on June 3, 2026, WCCF filed a Supplemental Statement

of Position, identifying the following links that would traverse or adversely affect lands owned or

managed by WCCF: F04, F4, F5, F6, F7, F43, and G9. The particular routes that would
 negatively impact Williamson County and WCCF are proposed routes 295, 296, and 572.

Williamson County and WCCF object to these particular routes and any route that would

incorporate any of the aforementioned links for the following reasons, which are provided in

further detail in the prior Statements of Position.

           First, links F04, F4, F5, F6, F7, F43, and G9 would impact conservation lands associated

with the Williamson County Regional Habitat Conservation Plan (“RHCP”), environmentally

sensitive karst features (i.e. Cobb Cavern Karst Fauna Area), and habitat preserved for endangered

species under the Endangered Species Act (i.e. Hidden Springs Ranch Preserve). These links

would interfere with WCCF’s implementation of the RHCP and associated mitigation obligations

undertaken in coordination with the United States Fish and Wildlife Service (“USFWS”). During

the Hearing on the Merits, the Applicant Panel testified that karst features should be avoided on

the selected route due to construction constraints posed by karst features and the presence of

critical habitat.1 Additionally, other witnesses testified at the Hearing on the Mertis as to why it

would not be prudent or preferrable to select a route where sensitive karst features are present.

           Next, links B3, D2, E3, E4, F01, F02, F04, F7, F8, F24, F33, F34, F41, F42, F43, F44,

F45, G9, G11, G31, G41, and G81 would impact public roads, rights-of-way, transportation

corridors, and areas in which Williamson County has already invested substantial public resources

in roadway planning, engineering, design, and construction projects. These particular links would

seriously disrupt or impair Williamson County’s long-range transportation plans and in particular,

Williamson County’s “Corridor J” project, located in one of the County’s fastest growing areas.

Moreover, the links of concern would conflict with planned roadway expansions, future

transportation corridors, intersection improvements, drainage infrastructure, and mobility projects



1
    Tr. (Vol. 3) at 276:5-14 (Cooley Cross); Tr. (Vol. 3) at 277:13-25 (Marusak Cross).
 already incorporated into the County’s transportation framework. Williamson County has already

invested hundreds of millions of dollars into its transportation framework and the links of concern

put that substantial investment at risk.

          Importantly, during the Hearing on the Merits, the PUC Staff witness testified that it would

be prudent and good planning to avoid Williamson County’s transportation corridor altogether.2

PUC Staff’s witness testified that there would be vertical clearance issues with constructing a

transmission line over Highway 195.3 In particular, PUC Staff’s witness identified vertical

clearance issues on proposed route 296 and link F34.4 Attached hereto as “Exhibit A” is a map

depicting the specific links of concern, which demonstrate how the proposed links would impact

Williamson County or WCCF. “Exhibit A” was admitted into evidence in SOAH Order No. 31.

          For these reasons, Williamson County and WCCF would respectfully urge the Honorable

Administrative Law Judges to (1) not recommend proposed routes 295, 296, or 572 and (2) to

select a route that avoids the links of concern identified herein. Out of the 122 proposed routes in

the Application, Williamson County and WCCF would support the Applicants’ preferred route

894. Williamson County and WCCF appreciate the Honorable Administrative Law Judges’ time

and attention on this very important matter.
